expected_metric: Attributable completed purchases from checkout sessions after trust-signal placement is confirmed at payment-entry point
hypothesis: Placing a visible guarantee badge or trust signal immediately adjacent to the payment entry field (not just elsewhere on the page) produces measurably higher conversion rates — 32% in 11 days in a controlled test. Nebula's checkout-to-purchase gap is most likely addressable by placement of guarantee language at the exact payment decision point, not elsewhere on the funnel.
observed_problem: Nebula has 19 checkout starts and 0 completed purchases. The current Stripe payment link is a bare checkout with no documented trust signals near the payment entry point — the highest-risk moment for cold first-time buyers.
smallest_safe_change: Audit the current checkout configuration for the presence of guarantee or security language immediately before the payment entry field; if absent, add a one-line guarantee statement at that placement and observe completion rate over the next 10 sessions.
stop_condition: Revert trust-signal placement if no improvement in checkout completion rate after 10 sessions
why_nebula: Nebula has no recorded trust signals at the payment entry point. This evidence identifies specific placement (near payment field, before 'Pay' button) as the critical variable — not just presence of a guarantee. This makes it a testable, reversible, config-level experiment.
